summary.text: 米 is a whole-graph picture of scattered grain. Its early referent was probably dehusked grain broadly; in modern usage it commonly means rice. The identity of the central stroke is disputed.

formation.text: Pictographic: the graph as a whole depicts scattered grain. Accounts disagree about whether the central stroke represents a sieve, a grain stalk, or another feature; identifying that stroke is not necessary to the overall grain-picture analysis.

history.text: Early forms are described as small marks above and below a central stroke. The selected oracle-bone-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact. Forms are also recorded for Chu manuscripts, bronze inscriptions, small seal script, and the Shuowen entry; one account reports that the marks began joining into strokes before small seal, with Chu examples showing that change was already underway. These descriptions do not establish a complete graphic sequence.

The Shuowen entry glosses 米 as grain seed and interprets its form as depicting the produce of a grain plant. This is an early dictionary interpretation, not independent confirmation of the graph’s origin.

uncertainties.text: The central stroke has been interpreted as a sieve or a grain stalk; it may instead be a non-specific separator. Its identity remains unresolved, though the overall grain-picture analysis does not depend on it.
The precise dates and contexts of reported early uses are unavailable here, and the chronology by which the broad grain sense became commonly rice-specific is unresolved.

senses.text: 米 is reported in oracle-bone use for rice or grain. Scholarly discussion identifies its early referent as probably dehusked grain broadly, rather than a single crop; the precise first-use date and inscription context are unresolved.
米 commonly means rice in modern usage.

In Japanese, 米 is used for the length unit metre following the use of 米突 to render French mètre by sound. This is a separate word use, unrelated in meaning to grain. The exact route by which 米 alone became current is unresolved.

developments.text: The broad early grain sense is commonly specialized to rice in modern usage, though when this change occurred is unresolved.

limitations.text: 米’s Japanese use for ‘metre’ is a graph borrowing: 米突 rendered French mètre by sound, after which 米 came to be used on its own. This does not show a semantic development from grain to a length unit; the date and precise route are unresolved.

Other reported early uses include writing 敉 ‘pacify’, a sacrificial name, and clan names. Their inscription contexts and relationship, if any, to the grain meaning are unresolved, so they are not treated as semantic developments or separate senses.
Other Japanese readings are listed, but their senses and histories are not explained here; only the metre use is supported by the cited account.

overview.text: 米 pictures scattered grain. Its early referent was probably dehusked grain broadly; today it commonly means rice. In Japanese it also writes “metre”: 米突 rendered French mètre by sound, and 米 later became a shorter spelling.
